title: Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act
official_title: To amend the Federal Reserve Act to prohibit the Federal reserve banks from offering certain products or services directly to an individual, to prohibit the use of central bank digital currency for monetary policy, and for other purposes.
summary: The Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act prohibits the Federal Reserve from creating, testing, or issuing any form of digital currency that would be a direct liability of the Fed and available to the general public. It also bans the Fed from using such a currency to conduct monetary policy. The ban covers both direct issuance and indirect issuance through banks or other intermediaries.
brief: Permanently prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing, testing, or using a central bank digital currency in any form, directly or through intermediaries.

top_lines.headline: Federal Reserve Banned from Issuing Digital Dollar
subs: Federal Reserve banks may not offer products or services directly to individuals, maintain individual accounts, or issue any central bank digital currency or substantially similar digital asset
Federal Reserve banks may not offer a central bank digital currency indirectly to individuals through financial institutions or other intermediaries
The Board of Governors may not test, study, develop, create, or implement a central bank digital currency

top_lines.headline: Monetary Policy Use Prohibited
subs: The Board of Governors and the Federal Open Market Committee may not use a central bank digital currency to implement monetary policy
Exception: open, permissionless, and private dollar-denominated digital currencies that fully preserve the privacy protections of physical cash are not prohibited

likelihoodReason: Passed the House 219-210 on a near-party-line vote with 2 Democratic crossovers and 135 Republican cosponsors. Faces the 60-vote Senate cloture threshold with 53 Republican senators; a partisan-line House record makes Senate advancement dependent on substantial Democratic crossover.

items.main: Names the Act the “Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Prohibition On Federal Reserve Banks Relating To Certain Products Or Services For Individuals And Prohibition On Directly Issuing A Central Bank Digital Currency

items.main: Amends section 16 of the Federal Reserve Act to bar a Federal reserve bank from offering products or services directly to an individual, maintaining an individual's account, or issuing a central bank digital currency (or substantially similar digital asset).
items.detail: Adds new paragraph (18); defines “central bank digital currency” by reference to section 10(11)(D).

sections.label: Section 3 — Prohibition On Federal Reserve Banks Indirectly Issuing A Central Bank Digital Currency

items.main: Further amends section 16 of the Federal Reserve Act to bar a Federal reserve bank from offering a central bank digital currency (or substantially similar digital asset) indirectly to an individual through a financial institution or other intermediary.
items.detail: Adds new paragraph (19); defines “central bank digital currency” by reference to section 10(11)(D).

sections.label: Section 4 — Prohibition With Respect To Central Bank Digital Currency

items.main: Amends section 10 of the Federal Reserve Act to bar the Board of Governors from testing, studying, developing, creating, or implementing a CBDC, and bars the Board and the Federal Open Market Committee from using a CBDC to implement monetary policy.
items.detail: Adds new paragraph (11). Exception preserves any dollar-denominated currency that is open, permissionless, and private and fully preserves the privacy protections of U.S. coins and physical currency. Defines CBDC as digital money/value that is denominated in the national unit of account, a direct liability of the Federal Reserve System, and widely available to the general public.

items.main: Expresses the sense of Congress that the Board of Governors currently lacks authority to issue a CBDC and will not have such authority unless Congress grants it under its Article 1, Section 8 powers.
items.detail: Sense-of-Congress statement — no substantive legal effect.

underreported.summary: Separately prohibits the Federal Reserve from offering a central bank digital currency indirectly through financial institutions or other intermediaries, in addition to the direct issuance prohibition in Section 2.
underreported.why_unreported: A two-tier central bank digital currency model — where the Fed issues a digital currency to commercial banks that then distribute it to customers — has been proposed in academic and policy contexts as a privacy-preserving alternative to direct Fed retail accounts. Section 3's separate prohibition on indirect issuance forecloses that design without discussing it in the bill's title or stated purpose.

gaps: The bill prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency but does not address whether the Treasury Department's existing coin and currency issuance authority could be used as an alternative legal path to a government-issued digital currency.

The bill defines a central bank digital currency as one that is a direct liability of the Federal Reserve and widely available to the general public, but does not define 'widely available' — leaving open the question of whether a wholesale central bank digital currency used only by financial institutions would be prohibited.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Steil
featured_quotes.text: He was actually one of the first in Congress to raise the alarm. Since then, the case has only grown stronger about the risks posed by U.S. CBDC. Mr. Speaker, the global economy is at a crossroads when it comes to digital payments. Jurisdictions around the world are upgrading their payment systems to be faster, to be cheaper, and cross-border. The private sector is leading the way, including payment stablecoins to enhance the payment rails. As the United States grapples with modernizing our own payment systems, we are confronted with a choice.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Lynch
featured_quotes.text: At the expense of U.S. global economic leadership, this misguided legislation would prevent the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency, also known as a CBDC. Unfortunately, the facts surrounding the development of CBDC have been obscured by disinformation, conspiracy theories, and extreme political ideology. Republicans and the crypto industry have made unfounded claims that a CBDC will be used as a surveillance tool by the Federal Government. Let's be clear about what a CBDC is.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Meuser
featured_quotes.text: This bill is about defending our Constitution and protecting the privacy of the American people. The Constitution is unambiguous in Article I, Section 8, which grants only Congress exclusive authority to coin money, regulate the value thereof, and of foreign coin. This is a clear provision of the United States Constitution. It is a foundational element of our constitutional Republic designed to keep such important authority over our Nation's currency issuance within the hands of the people's Representatives.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Rose
featured_quotes.text: Among the many rights that we enjoy as Americans, privacy is among the most fundamental. Establishing a central bank digital currency would not only usurp consumers' privacy and individual freedoms, but it would also hinder free market innovation. Digital assets are here to stay. I agree strongly with President Trump that the United States should be a leader in this space. However, the last administration held a very different view.

added: Prohibition on Federal Reserve banks offering products or services directly to individuals
Prohibition on Federal Reserve banks maintaining individual accounts
Prohibition on Federal Reserve banks issuing a central bank digital currency directly or through intermediaries
Prohibition on the Board of Governors testing, studying, developing, or implementing a central bank digital currency
Prohibition on using a central bank digital currency for monetary policy
modified: Federal Reserve Act Section 16: two new paragraphs (18 and 19) added banning direct and indirect central bank digital currency issuance
Federal Reserve Act Section 10: new paragraph banning central bank digital currency testing, development, and monetary policy use
Direct-offering prohibition narrowed from "products or services" to "financial products or services" directly to an individual (Sec. 2, new paragraph (18)(A)(i))
